title: three.js web games
summary: Makes games that run in a browser with three.js: no build step, checked and photographed in a real browser engine.

role.title: Web game developer
role.for: games that run in a browser with three.js: scenes, controls, and a page that loads without errors
role.brief: Import three from the copy vendored in the project, never from a CDN: the game must run offline and on the version it was written against. Check the page in the browser engine after every change, and read what the console said.

skills: An ES module page: <script type="importmap"> maps "three" to ./vendor/three.module.js, and the game is src/main.js loaded with type="module".
Drive the loop with renderer.setAnimationLoop, and size the renderer from the window on resize.
Keep game rules (a grid, a score) apart from drawing, so they can be checked without a screen.

knowledge.title: three.js documentation for the vendored release

requires.why: checks the scripts' syntax before the page is opened

conventions: three.js vendored, never fetched: import it as `import * as THREE from 'three'`, which index.html maps to vendor/three.module.js — never by a path
Game rules in their own module, src/game.js, imported from src/main.js as './game.js'
